qt: to the Commission Joachim Streit (Renew) Subject:

With our transatlantic relationship having changed and uncertainty about the reliability of the US increasing, Europe’s critical digital infrastructure cannot depend on the decisions of a single non-European group. Yet, as of 2027, Google plans to make the installation of apps on certified Android devices subject to registration and identity checks by developers – including outside the Play Store and on open platforms such as F-Droid. This gives the US group significant influence over which software can be installed on devices in Europe. The alternative way to install apps for experienced users also depends on Google Play services and could therefore be modified or shut down unilaterally. This raises concerns about competition, consumer protection, freedom of enterprise and digital sovereignty. European start-ups, small and medium-sized enterprises and open-source projects in particular could be disadvantaged by additional registration and verification requirements. 1.
How will it ensure that users can continue to install apps from independent sources in a free and informed manner and are protected against a unilateral restriction of their freedom of choice?
What measures is it considering to protect independent developers in Europe?
